summary: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Geshe degree at Menri Monastery and studied under teachers including Sangye Tenzin and Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak. He held posts at Menri, LTWA (~1986–1989), and Rice University (1991).

Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison before serving on the faculty at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

Terese Tse Bartholomew specializes in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology. After earning an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles, she served at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco, including as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art (attested 2001–2003).
Tertön Sogyal was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He was also a teacher of the 13th Dalai Lama.

Teruji Ishizu was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). He held posts at Nihon University, Tohoku University (including president, 1963–1966), Miyagi University of Education (president, 1965), Keio University, and Komazawa University.

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz specialized in religious and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Florida State University and the University of Virginia (PhD). She taught Hindi at Virginia, religious studies at Indiana University Indianapolis (~1991–2001), and served as Professor of Religion at Florida State (1993).
Tessa Verney Wheeler was a scholar in history and archaeology. She was educated at Addey and Stanhope School (1905–1911) and University College London (1911–1914).

Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He held professorships at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University (attested 1972), and served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1970–1982).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University under teachers Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue was a philosopher and religious scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Heidelberg, Leipzig, and Berlin under teachers including Kuno Fischer and Wilhelm Wundt. He held professorships and deanships at the University of Tokyo, Toyo University, and Daito Bunka University.

Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He held numerous leadership posts, serving as professor and president of Komazawa University (president 2002–2006), and later as president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

Tetsuro Noguchi was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. Over his career, he held academic posts at Yokohama National University (~1967–1978), the University of Tsukuba (~1978–1996), and J. F. Oberlin University (~1996–2003).

Tetsuro Watsuji was a philosopher, Japanologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, he studied under Martin Heidegger and Natsume Sōseki, later holding ethics chairs at Kyoto University (1931–1934) and the University of Tokyo (1934–1949).

Tetsuzo Tanikawa was a philosopher who studied at the First Higher School and Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Doshisha University (~1928–1938) and served as a professor at Hosei University (~1938–1965).

Teun Goudriaan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He held academic appointments at Utrecht University, where he was attested as a committee member in 1989 and as Professor Emeritus in 2000.
Thanissaro Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oberlin College and trained under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko. He founded the Metta Forest Monastery and became its abbot in 1993.
Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under guide V. D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

Theodor Aufrecht was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of Berlin. He served as a Privatdozent at Berlin, held a post at the Bodleian Library, and was a professor at Edinburgh (1861–1875) and Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist educated at the University of Göttingen, where he completed his Ph.D. and Habilitation. He spent his academic career at Göttingen, serving as Privatdozent, Lehrmeister, and ultimately Ordinarius professor from 1862 to 1881.

Theodor Bloch was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch (~1888–1892) and later pursued specialized studies under Georg Bühler (~1893–1895).
